cells.tense: You are here right now, and the want and the move are running together.
cells.ask: Finish one thing already rolling and let it stand without checking it again.
cells.core:
Feeling and direction are running together. You want what you're doing and you're doing it. It doesn't feel forced and it doesn't feel like dragging. The momentum is quiet — you've stopped needing to convince yourself or anyone else that it's real.

How things work underneath is easy for you to see right now. That view is worth something on its own. It also means one thing can be finished without being audited a third time. Pick the piece that's already moving and bring it to a close. The stillness after that is yours to keep, not a problem to solve.

cells.tense: You are living ahead of yourself, bracing for a future you cannot write in.
cells.ask: Pause one plan and say what it's actually for, out loud, before you move it again.
cells.core:
You are already in the next room. The plan is three steps ahead of where anything actually is — you've felt how it should go, so you're pushing the present to catch up. The pace that used to feel natural has speed on it now, and it's carrying you past the thing you were trying to enjoy.

How things work underneath is easy for you to read, which is exactly why you keep adding moves. Bring one plan back to the table and say what it's for — not the next version, just the reason it started. If the reason still holds, you'll know how to move. If it doesn't, you've saved yourself the sprint.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door you already crossed, not walking through it.
cells.ask: Do one small piece of the thing you keep describing, and let that be enough for today.
cells.core:
Feeling and direction came apart at some point, and you stopped moving toward what you wanted. You still want it — you can hear it when you talk about the thing. But the line between wanting it and doing it got cut, and you've been standing on the wanting side of it.

How things work underneath is easy for you to see, but seeing hasn't moved you. That's fine, it doesn't have to. Pick one small piece of the thing you keep describing and do just that. Not for the result — for the motion. If it feels like nothing, that's still motion, and the signal will take it.

cells.tense: You are writing this direction in real time, and not calling it yours.
cells.ask: Before the next step, say out loud which choice was yours and which was momentum's.
cells.core:
The direction you're in has your fingerprints on it — the way you kept going, the way you chose not to. But you keep describing it as just how things went, the way things carried you. The writing is happening, and you haven't claimed the room yet.

How things work underneath is easy for you to read cold, which makes it simple to call the pattern the author and yourself the observer. One move changes that: before the next step, name which choice was yours and which belonged to momentum. You don't need to decide how it feels. You just need to sign the part you wrote.
cells.sheetLine: You're already writing this direction. You just haven't signed it.
